ABSTRACT
In the field of cognitive networks, particularly within the Internet of Things and wireless sensor networks, secure and energy-­
efficient data transmission is crucial. Traditional methods often fall short in optimizing energy and enhancing security during 
data transmission. Effective key management schemes that are both secure and energy-­efficient are still lacking. Moreover, many 
challenges remain based on high computational overhead, diversity, low throughout, and latency issues, which lead to poor 
performance. To find the solution for aforementioned issues, this research proposes a novel Multipath Link Routing Protocol 
for secure and energy-­aware data transmission, leveraging optimal cluster head selection within cognitive Internet of Things-­
wireless sensor networks applications. The sensor data is collected from the environment using sensor nodes. The novel Hybrid 
Pelican Optimization Algorithm based Sine Cosine Algorithm is suggested to choose optimal clusters during cluster generation. 
In this, the Sine Cosine Algorithm is integrated into the Pelican Optimization Algorithm to mitigate diversity challenges and 
ensure proper balancing. Then, the Multipath Link Routing Protocol approach implements numerous paths for dependable and 
effective data transfer across sensor nodes. Here, pair wise keys are shared by Multipath Link Routing Protocol approach be-
tween adjacent nodes to guarantee secure transmission. Additionally, the implementation of homomorphic encryption technique 
encrypts and decrypts messages to address the key distribution issue for securing transmission during secret key generation. 
Furthermore, data degradation and retransmission are avoided by this protocol, which uses query, routing request, and route 
reply to identify the routing from source node to destination node. After that, the creation of a blockchain-­assisted authentica-
tion framework ensures safe access while guarding against illegal access in cloud-­stored data. By encrypting the input data, the 
hash function applies SHA 512 to generate hash value in blockchain technology. The objective is to create a routing protocol that 
maximizes the effectiveness of data sharing while taking into account the intrinsic limits of sensor nodes such as computing and 
energy limitations. By using performance metrics like throughput, latency, and energy efficiency, the system achieves its goals. 
Compared to prior secure data transmission approaches, the proposed approach attains greater findings of 98.15% throughput, 
110-­J energy consumption, 87-­ms latency, and 98.59% security rate, where the values are greater than other techniques. The sim-
ulation findings indicate that the proposed approach successfully improves security and energy efficiency for data transmission 
in cognitive Internet of Things and wireless sensor networks.

1   |   Introduction
The emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and wireless 
sensor networks (WSNs) has revolutionized data acquisition, 
processing, and transmission in various fields such as smart 
cities, healthcare, industrial automation, and environmental 
monitoring. IoT involves embedding physical objects with 
computing capabilities, enabling effortless and automatic 
data transfer between devices [1]. IoT environments typi-
cally comprise four types of entities including cloud storage 
servers, edge gateways, and various IoT devices and users. 
Examples of real-­time IoT applications encompass smart 
homes, healthcare, urban life, shopping and commerce, farm-
ing, transportation, and border protection [2]. WSN consists of 
distributed sensor nodes that collect environmental data and 
transmit it to a target node for analysis. There are two types 
of WSNs:wireless aboveground sensor networks (WASN) and 
wireless underground sensor networks (WUSN) [3]. A new 
wireless communications paradigm called cognitive radio 
(CR) aims to make effective use of the spectrum. WSNs and 
CR are combined to create a cognitive WSN (CWSN), which 
successfully addresses the spectrum resource scarcity issues 
in WSNs [4]. Using dynamic spectrum access (DSA), CR al-
lows secondary users (SUs) to use opportunistic idle licensed 
spectrum without interfering with primary users (PUs) [5]. 
This effectively addresses the issue of a lack of available spec-
trum sources and significantly increases spectrum utilization.
Clustering is a widely used approach to reduce energy consump-
tion by reducing redundant data transmission (DT) between 
nodes. In this approach, sensor nodes are grouped into clusters, 
each managed by a cluster head (CH) responsible for commu-
nicating with other cluster members and the base station (BS) 
[6]. Optimal CH selection is essential for energy efficiency and 
network longevity, and various optimization algorithms such 
as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Artificial Bee Colony 
(ABC), and Golden Jackal Optimization (GJO) have been pro-
posed to select the optimal CH. IoT faces significant challenges 
related to data security, reliability, and privacy [7]. Safety mech-
anisms such as strong authentication and data encryption are 
essential to stopping unauthorized access. Lightweight encryp-
tion methods such as block and stream ciphers are suitable for 
resource-­constrained sensor nodes. Despite traditional security 
mechanisms, WSNs remain vulnerable to attacks, especially 
insider attacks. Trust-­based security mechanisms have been 
introduced to counter these insider threats, as they rely on 
the cooperation and trustworthiness of nodes in the network 
[8]. Clustering and optimal CH selection play an important 
role in reducing energy consumption and improving network 
performance.
Existing research has addressed several aspects of secure DT 
in WSNs and IoT. Traditional cryptographic techniques have 
been employed to enhance data confidentiality and integrity, 
but these methods often demand high computational and 
energy resources, which are unsuitable for resource-­limited 
sensor nodes [9]. Moreover, the integration of cognitive ca-
pabilities introduces additional challenges such as managing 
spectrum availability, mitigating interference, and ensuring 
seamless communication in the presence of malicious nodes. 
Advanced frameworks are needed to address issues such as 
limited scalability, lack of compatibility with network dynam-
ics, and adequate mechanisms to balance energy efficiency 
and security [10]. Blockchain technology has recently gained 
attention as a potential solution for enhancing security in cog-
nitive IoT-­WSNs by providing a decentralized, tamper-­proof 
framework for data validation and transmission [11]. However, 
its application is hindered by the computational overhead 
and energy consumption associated with traditional block-
chain architectures. The existing Movement Optimization for 
Cyborg Cockroach approach does not address the critical as-
pects of secure DT and energy efficiency, which are essential 
for practical IoT-­WSN applications [12]. To overcome these 
limitations, there is a pressing need for novel approaches that 
combine advanced optimization techniques with blockchain 
to ensure both energy efficiency and robust security. In hier-
archical routing, which is more energy efficient than flat rout-
ing, sensor nodes send data to the sink node via intermediate 
CHs [13]. This method increases network lifetime and ensures 
efficient data transfer. However, the challenges of proper CH 
allocation and energy consumption minimization in CHs re-
main active research areas. The proposed novel Multipath 
Link Routing Protocol (MLRP) addresses these challenges in 
this secure and energy-­aware DT research. These contribu-
tions to transmit data energy efficiently and securely in cogni-
tive IoT-­WSN are as follows:
•	 Objective: The research proposes a novel MLRP ap-
proach for secure and energy-­aware DT in cognitive IoT-­
WSN. This protocol facilitates optimal CH selection and 
implements multipath routes for dependable and effective 
data transfer, addressing the limitations of traditional 
methods.
•	 Data collection and Optimal CH Selection: Sensor nodes 
are employed to gather data from the surroundings and 
then transmit it to the CH generation phase. To mitigate di-
versity and balancing challenges in cognitive networks, the 
integrated Hybrid Pelican Optimization Algorithm-­based 
Sine Cosine Algorithm (Hybrid POA-­SCA) is suggested for 
selecting optimal CHs.
•	 Secure routing: The MLRP approach establishes several 
routes across sensor nodes to transmit data efficiently and 
securely. In addition, the MLRP approach enhances safe 
transmission by distributing pairwise keys among neigh-
boring nodes, enabling encrypted and decrypted DT to 
guarantee confidentiality and integrity. Public key cryptog-
raphy encrypts and decrypts messages to solve the issues of 
key distribution for secure channels.
•	 Route maintenance: The purpose of route maintenance is 
to find some alternative routes. Here, the usage of query, 
routing request, and route reply messages in the MLRP 
approach helps avoid data degradation and retransmission 
while identifying the route from the source node to the des-
tination node.
•	 User authentication: For ensuring secure access and 
preventing unauthorized access, blockchain-­centered au-
thentication system is implemented to protect data stored 
on the cloud. The SHA-­512 hashing algorithm is applied to 
generate hash value in Blockchain (BC) technology through 
encrypting input data.

Kingston Roberts and Thangavel [14] demonstrated a Residual-­
Energy-­based Data Availability technique (REDAA) for the pur-
pose of enhancing lifetime of networks by employing CHs as well 
as stable routing path selection. Once the path was formalized, 
based upon the request the data were available by creating two 
kinds of CHs. Moreover, this mechanism acquired best through-
put value. Karthick [3] developed an Energy-­aware Reliable 
Medium Access Control (EARMAC) approach that was applied 
to communicate data energy-­efficiently and dependably in WSN. 
Clusters were created within the geographical area, and each 
cluster's leader node was chosen according to a set of criteria. The 
destination node received the information from the leader nodes 
via the proper multi-­hop communication approach and it achieved 
data dependability while avoiding needless control overhead.
Han et al. [15] presented an adaptive genetic approach (TAGA) 
to less energy consumption DT in WSN. A threshold function

2.4   |   Limitations and Research Gap
Previous research works demonstrated in terms of security 
and energy-­aware DT systems have significant influence on 
the cognitive IoT-­WSN field. However, there were still many 
obstacles and constraints regarding ensuring secure data 
transfer and minimizing energy use, therefore need for further 
research. The following highlights the difficulties in the pre-
vious research: Many existing approaches struggle to balance 
security with energy efficiency. Effective key management 
schemes that were both secure and energy-­efficient were still 
lacking. Ensuring low-­latency transmission, while maintaining 
high security and energy efficiency was difficult. Many solu-
tions increase latency due to the added overhead of security 
protocols. Moreover, many challenges remain based on high 
computational overhead, diversity, low throughout, poor en-
ergy efficiency, and end-­to-­end delay issues, which lead to poor 
performance. The gaps in earlier secure and energy-­aware DT 
research were filled by the proposed mechanism. To overcome 
these challenges, the MLRP approach is introduced in this re-
search which enhances the energy efficiency and throughput for 
securely transmitting data in cognitive IoT-­WSN. Additionally, 
the diversity and balancing issues are reduced by selecting CHs 
using integrated Hybrid POA-­SCA to reduce latency and end-­
to-­end delay. The homomorphic encryption technique encrypts 
and decrypts messages to address the key distribution issue for 
safe transmission and BC assisted authentication framework 
guarantees safe access while guarding against unauthorized 
access in cloud-­stored data.

protocol that maximizes data-­sharing efficiency while mini-

throughput, latency, and energy consumption.

3.2   |   Problem Formulation
The primary challenge in secure routing within cognitive IoT-­
WSN environments is to establish a reliable method for private 
DT between sensor nodes while mitigating risks associated with 
wormhole attacks and ensuring robust data security. The objec-
tive is to design a routing protocol that optimizes data-­sharing 
efficiency, considering the inherent limitations of sensor nodes, 
such as energy and computational constraints.
The WSN is denoted by W = (N, C), where sensor node set is rep-
resented by N, and C represents the communication link set be-
tween nodes. The objective is to discover secure routing protocol 
(ℜ) that guarantees secure private IoT DT while reducing the

message is created to alert another node to a link breakage, 
should a node fail to get a Hello message from a neighboring 
node within a designated time period known as the Hello in-

6.1   |   Security Analysis and Threat Model
Ensuring secure DT in cognitive IoT-­WSN environments is cru-
cial for protecting sensitive information and maintaining net-
work integrity. The proposed MLRP protocol achieves a security 
rate of 98.59%, which is validated through simulations that test 
its resilience against various potential threats. This section pro-
vides a detailed security analysis by examining how the proto-
col resists specific types of attacks and evaluates its robustness 
using a defined threat model.
•	 Threat model
The threat model considers a range of potential attacks that 
cognitive IoT-­WSN environments are prone to. These include:
1.	 Man-­in-­the-­Middle (MitM) Attack: An adversary in-
tercepts and potentially alters communication between 
two nodes.
2.	 Replay Attack: Captured legitimate packets are retrans-
mitted to disrupt routing or impersonate nodes.
3.	 Wormhole Attack: Malicious nodes create a direct link 
(tunnel) to manipulate routing and compromise DT.
4.	 Sybil Attack: A single node impersonates multiple iden-
tities to disrupt network operations or influence routing 
decisions.
5.	 Denial of Service (DoS) Attack: The network is flooded 
with excessive traffic, depleting resources and disrupting 
normal operations.
•	 Resistance to attacks
The MLRP protocol is designed with robust security mecha-
nisms to address these threats effectively.
1. Man-­in-­the-­Middle (MitM) Attack:
•	 Defense Mechanism: The protocol uses homomorphic 
encryption to secure DT between nodes. Each data packet 
is encrypted with a pairwise key generated during route 
setup. Without access to the private keys, an adversary can-
not decrypt the data even if they intercept it.
•	 Role of Blockchain: The blockchain ensures data integrity

Initially, sensor nodes are used to gather data from the sur-
roundings and then transmit it to the CH generation phase. 
Secondly, the optimal CH is chosen by employing the Hybrid 
Pelican Optimisation Algorithm-­based Sine Cosine Algorithm 
(Hybrid POA-­SCA) to generate clusters. Here, the POA faces

proper balancing. After that, MLRP enhances safe transmission 
by distributing pairwise keys among neighboring nodes, en-

ity and integrity. Key distribution challenges are mitigated by 
public key cryptography technique to provide secure channels.

destination using control messages including Route Request, 
Route Reply, Route Error, and HELLO messages. Finally, data

assisted authentication system. The SHA-­512 hashing algorithm

Abstract: In the field of cognitive networks, particularly within the Internet of Things and wireless sensor networks, secure and energy-­ efficient data transmission is crucial. Traditional methods often fall short in optimizing energy and enhancing security during data transmission. Effective key management schemes that are both secure and energy-­efficient are still lacking. Moreover, many challenges remain based on high computational overhead, diversity, low throughout, and latency issues, which lead to poor performance. To find the solution for aforementioned issues, this research proposes a novel Multipath Link Routing Protocol for secure and energy-­aware data transmission, leveraging optimal cluster head selection within cognitive Internet of Things-­ wireless sensor networks applications. The sensor data is collected from the environment using sensor nodes. The novel Hybrid Pelican Optimization Algorithm based Sine Cosine Algorithm is suggested to choose optimal clusters during cluster generation. In this, the Sine Cosine Algorithm is integrated into the Pelican Optimization Algorithm to mitigate diversity challenges and ensure proper balancing. Then, the Multipath Link Routing Protocol approach implements numerous paths for dependable and effective data transfer across sensor nodes. Here, pair wise keys are shared by Multipath Link Routing Protocol approach be- tween adjacent nodes to guarantee secure transmission. Additionally, the implementation of homomorphic encryption technique encrypts and decrypts messages to address the key distribution issue for securing transmission during secret key generation. Furthermore, data degradation and retransmission are avoided by this protocol, which uses query, routing request, and route reply to identify the routing from source node to destination node. After that, the creation of a blockchain-­assisted authentica- tion framework ensures safe access while guarding against illegal access in cloud-­stored data. By encrypting the input data, the hash function applies SHA 512 to generate hash value in blockchain technology. The objective is to create a routing protocol that maximizes the effectiveness of data sharing while taking into account the intrinsic limits of sensor nodes such as computing and energy limitations. By using performance metrics like throughput, latency, and energy efficiency, the system achieves its goals. Compared to prior secure data transmission approaches, the proposed approach attains greater findings of 98.15% throughput, 110-­J energy consumption, 87-­ms latency, and 98.59% security rate, where the values are greater than other techniques.
